ORIGIN.quote: The labels are suggestive—`OpenAIBot`, `OpenAIResearcher`, `AgentMassPointer13`, `LinkHelper771`—but labels are user-controlled and therefore weak identity evidence.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader sees plenty of OpenAI-flavoured artefacts (OpenAIBot, OpenAIResearcher, AgentTestOpenAI…, AgentChatGPT…, "OAI coordination", OpenAIMassValuesJune20Master) and one brief remark that such labels are weak identity evidence, but the report never proposes OpenAI — or any lab — as a candidate operator or source of the swarm; the labels are invoked only to argue about whether the actors are agents versus scripts, and the closing line about "names that look like product or research identities" dismisses them without ever naming the inference. That partial framing of the names as (unreliable) identity evidence lifts it above pure 0.2 silence, but because OpenAI is never put on the table as a possible origin to be set aside, it falls short of the 0.4 explicit-refusal band.
